literal: Death was kept secret; Palace Attendant Zong Ai forged the Empress's order, killed Prince of Dongping Han, welcomed Prince of Nan'an Yu inward and set him up, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the reign title to Yongping, and honored Empress Helian as Empress Dowager.
idiomatic: Death was kept secret; Zong Ai forged the Empress's order, killed Han, Prince of Dongping, welcomed Yu, Prince of Nan'an, proclaimed amnesty, changed the title to Yongping, and honored Empress Helian as Empress Dowager.

literal: Third month, day xinmao: the posthumous title Taiwu Emperor was raised; burial was at Yunzhong Jinling; temple name Shizu.
idiomatic: In the third month, on the xinmao day, the posthumous title Emperor Taiwu was raised; he was buried at Yunzhong Jinling; temple name Shizu.

literal: Summer, sixth month: Liu Yilong's general Tan Hezhi raided Jizhou; Liang Tan and Lu Ansheng encamped at Jingsuo; Pang Meng and Xue Andu raided Hongnong.
idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer Tan Hezhi of Liu Yilong raided Jizhou; Liang Tan and Lu Ansheng camped at Jingsuo; Pang Meng and Xue Andu raided Hongnong.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: General Who Conquers the South, Duke of Anding Han Yuanxing campaigned against them; Hezhi withdrew, and Liang Tan and Ansheng also fled.
idiomatic: In the seventh month Han Yuanxing, Duke of Anding, General Who Conquers the South, campaigned against them; Hezhi withdrew and Liang Tan and Ansheng fled.

literal: Eighth month: General Who Vanquishes the Foe Feng Li led two thousand horse south across from Fuzhou Ford toward Hongnong.
idiomatic: In the eighth month Feng Li, General Who Vanquishes the Foe, led two thousand horse south from Fuzhou Ford toward Hongnong.

literal: Ninth month: Minister of Works, Duke of Gaoping Erwugan encamped at Tong Pass; General Who Pacifies the South, Duke of Changli Yuan Liao, encamped at Henei.
idiomatic: In the ninth month Erwugan, Duke of Gaoping, Minister of Works, encamped at Tong Pass; Yuan Liao, Duke of Changli, General Who Pacifies the South, at Henei.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day bingwu, first day: Yu was murdered by Zong Ai.
idiomatic: On the new-year bingwu day of the tenth month of winter Yu was murdered by Zong Ai.

literal: Palace Attendant Changsun Kehou of the Secretariat and Minister of Works Lu Li welcomed and set up the imperial grandson—this is Emperor Gaozong.
idiomatic: Changsun Kehou, Palace Attendant, and Lu Li, Minister of Works, welcomed the imperial grandson—Emperor Gaozong.

literal: The Emperor never knew Empress Mi in life; when he came to awareness he spoke with grief and moved those beside him; Taizong heard and praised him.
idiomatic: He never knew Empress Mi in life; when he came to awareness he grieved aloud and moved those beside him; Taizong heard and praised him.

literal: When Taizong was unwell he did not remove his belt.
idiomatic: When Taizong was ill he did not remove his belt.

literal: By nature he was pure, frugal, and plain; dress, carriage, food, and drink were only what sufficed; he did not love rarities; he ate no second dish; the favored Ladies of Bright Deportment and Honored Persons wore no multicolored robes.
idiomatic: He was pure and frugal; dress and food sufficed; he loved no luxuries, ate but one dish, and favored consorts wore no multicolored robes.

literal: The ministers reported to the Emperor that the capital walls and moat should be heightened further, following the Changes in the meaning of setting defenses, and also cited Xiao He's argument for magnificence.
idiomatic: Ministers urged heightening the capital walls per the Changes and cited Xiao He's plea for magnificence.

literal: The Emperor said: "The ancients had a saying: virtue lies not in defenses.
idiomatic: The Emperor said: "The ancients said virtue lies not in defenses.

literal: Juqu Qufu steamed earth to build a city, yet We destroyed him—was it in the walls?
idiomatic: Juqu Qufu built walls of steamed earth and We destroyed him—was it the walls?

literal: The realm is not yet pacified and We still need the people's strength; earthworks We have not undertaken; Xiao He's reply is not elegant speech."
idiomatic: The realm is not pacified and We need the people's strength; We have not built walls; Xiao He's reply is not fine speech."

literal: He always held wealth the root of army and state and spent nothing lightly; even in reward it was only households of those who died in service for merit—kinsmen favored never received anything beyond measure.
idiomatic: He held wealth the root of army and state and spent lightly on nothing; rewards went only to families of the dead in merit—kin never received beyond measure.

literal: Facing the enemy he was always with the soldiers amid arrows and stones; those beside him were wounded and killed in succession, yet the Emperor's expression was calm—therefore men wished to give their lives and wherever he turned nothing stood before him.
idiomatic: In battle he stood with the soldiers under arrow and stone; aides fell beside him yet his face was calm—men gave their lives and nothing stood before him.

literal: When he ordered generals forth he assigned strategy; those who obeyed were never not victorious; those who deviated mostly met defeat.
idiomatic: He assigned strategy to generals; obedience won; deviation mostly lost.

literal: By nature he also knew men and raised officers from the ranks, using only their talent and effectiveness without regard to origin.
idiomatic: He knew men and raised officers from the ranks for talent alone, regardless of origin.

literal: Moreover he was very stern and clear in punishments and rewards.
idiomatic: He was stern and clear in punishments and rewards.

literal: The meritorious were rewarded without omitting even enemies;
idiomatic: The meritorious were rewarded without omitting even enemies;

literal: the guilty were punished without avoiding kin; even those he favored were never excused from the law.
idiomatic: the guilty were punished without sparing kin; even favorites were never excused.

literal: He often said: "The law is what We share with the realm—how dare We treat it lightly?"
idiomatic: He often said: "The law is Ours with the realm—how dare We treat it lightly?"

literal: Therefore when great ministers violated the law there was no indulgence.
idiomatic: When great ministers broke the law there was no indulgence.

literal: He excelled at listening and observing; in an instant subordinates could not hide their treachery.
idiomatic: He listened and observed keenly; in an instant subordinates could not hide treachery.

literal: Yet he was resolute in execution and afterward often repented.
idiomatic: Yet he was quick to kill and often repented afterward.

literal: After Chancellor of State Cui Hao died, the Emperor campaigned north; at that time Duke of Xuancheng Li Xiaobo was gravely ill and rumor said he had died.
idiomatic: After Cui Hao died the Emperor campaigned north; Li Xiaobo, Duke of Xuancheng, was gravely ill and rumor said he had died.

literal: The Emperor heard and mourned him, saying to those beside him: "Li of Xuancheng is to be regretted."
idiomatic: Hearing this he mourned and said: "Li of Xuancheng is to be regretted."

literal: He also said: "We spoke wrongly before."
idiomatic: He also said: "We spoke wrongly before."

literal: Cui the Chancellor is to be regretted; Li of Xuancheng is to be pitied."
idiomatic: Chancellor Cui is to be regretted; Li of Xuancheng is to be pitied."

literal: In praise and blame his refined intent was all of this kind.
idiomatic: His praise and blame were all of this kind.

literal: Emperor Jingmu Gongzong bore the taboo name Huang; he was the Taiwu Emperor's eldest son; his mother was Lady He.
idiomatic: Emperor Jingmu Gongzong bore the taboo name Huang; he was the Taiwu Emperor's eldest son; his mother was Lady He.

literal: Yanhe year 1, spring, first month, day bingwu: he was established as Crown Prince at age five.
idiomatic: In Yanhe year 1, on the bingwu day of the first month of spring, he was made Crown Prince at five.

literal: Bright and intelligent with strong memory; what he heard he did not forget.
idiomatic: Bright and strong of memory; he forgot nothing he heard.

literal: When he grew he loved reading the classics and histories and all grasped their great meaning.
idiomatic: Grown, he loved the classics and histories and grasped their great meaning.

literal: Shizu marveled at him.
idiomatic: Shizu marveled at him.

literal: When Shizu campaigned east against Helong, an edict ordered Gongzong to record Secretariat affairs;
idiomatic: When Shizu campaigned east on Helong, Gongzong was ordered to record Secretariat affairs;

literal: when he campaigned west on Liangzhou, an edict ordered Gongzong to oversee the realm.
idiomatic: when he campaigned west on Liangzhou, Gongzong was ordered to oversee the realm.

literal: Earlier, when Shizu campaigned on Hexi, Li Shun and others all said Guzang had no grass or water and an army could not march.
idiomatic: Earlier, campaigning on Hexi, Li Shun and others said Guzang had no grass or water and no army could march.

literal: Gongzong showed doubt.
idiomatic: Gongzong looked doubtful.

literal: When the imperial carriage reached Guzang, an edict was sent to Gongzong: "East and west of Guzang city spring water joins north of the city, large as a river.
idiomatic: At Guzang he edicted Gongzong: "East and west of Guzang springs join north of the city, large as a river.

literal: The rest flow through ditches into marshes; between them there is no dry ground.
idiomatic: Ditches flow into marshes; between them is no dry ground.

literal: Marsh grass is lush and can supply a great army for several years.
idiomatic: Marsh grass is lush and can feed a great army for years.

literal: Much talk by men is also hateful.
idiomatic: Men's much talk is hateful too.

literal: Therefore this edict, to dispel your doubt."
idiomatic: Hence this edict to dispel your doubt."

literal: Gongzong said to the palace ministers: "To be a minister so untrue as this—is this loyalty?
idiomatic: Gongzong told palace ministers: "A minister so untrue—is this loyalty?

literal: When I first heard I had doubt, but the Emperor had decided to march.
idiomatic: I doubted at first, but the Emperor had decided to march.

literal: Nearly to err in a great matter—how can the speakers face the Emperor again?"
idiomatic: Nearly to err in a great matter—how can the speakers face the Emperor again?"

literal: Zhenjun year 4: Gongzong followed Shizu against the Rouran to Luhun Valley; they met the enemy; the barbarians were fearful and the tribes were disturbed.
idiomatic: In Zhenjun year 4 Gongzong followed Shizu against the Rouran to Luhun Valley; they met the enemy; the tribes were thrown into disorder.

literal: Gongzong said to Shizu: "Now the great army has come suddenly; we should press the attack swiftly and take them unawares—breaking them is certain."
idiomatic: Gongzong said: "The great army has come suddenly; press the attack and take them unawares—victory is certain."

literal: Minister of Works Liu Jie firmly remonstrated, holding that the dust was great and the enemy many; if they went out to level ground they might be surrounded; the army must gather in full before striking.
idiomatic: Liu Jie, Minister of Works, remonstrated: the dust was great and enemies many; on level ground they might be surrounded; wait for the full host.

literal: Gongzong said to Jie: "This dust is great because the enemy are frightened and the soldiers are in disorder—how could there be such dust over a camp?"
idiomatic: Gongzong said: "The dust is from enemy panic and soldier disorder—how dust over a camp?"

literal: Shizu doubted and did not press the attack swiftly; the Rouran fled far.
idiomatic: Shizu doubted and did not press; the Rouran fled far.

literal: Later Rouran scouts were captured; Shizu questioned them; they replied: "The Rouran did not know the army had come suddenly; all were fearful and led the host north; after six or seven days, knowing there was no pursuit, they went slowly."
idiomatic: Captured scouts said: "The Rouran did not know the army had come; all fled north; after six or seven days without pursuit they went slowly."

literal: Shizu deeply regretted it; from then on Gongzong's words on army and state were mostly adopted and he came to know the myriad affairs.
idiomatic: Shizu deeply regretted it; thereafter Gongzong's counsel on army and state was mostly followed and he came to know the myriad affairs.

literal: Earlier, when Gongzong oversaw the realm, he issued an order: "The Zhou Documents say: 'Entrust the farmer with plowing and tribute of the nine grains;
idiomatic: Earlier, overseeing the realm, he ordered: "The Zhou Documents say: 'Entrust the farmer with plowing and tribute of the nine grains;

literal: entrust the gardener with trees and tribute of plants and trees;
idiomatic: entrust the gardener with trees and tribute of plants;

literal: entrust the artisan with surplus materials and tribute of vessels;
idiomatic: entrust the artisan with surplus materials and tribute of vessels;

literal: [6] entrust the merchant with market affairs and tribute of goods and wealth;
idiomatic: [6] entrust the merchant with market affairs and tribute of goods;

literal: entrust the herdsman with livestock and tribute of birds and beasts;
idiomatic: entrust the herdsman with livestock and tribute of birds and beasts;

literal: entrust the consort with women's work and tribute of cloth and silk;
idiomatic: entrust the consort with women's work and tribute of cloth;

literal: entrust the forest officer with mountain affairs and tribute of its materials;
idiomatic: entrust the forest officer with mountain affairs and tribute of materials;

literal: entrust the park officer with marsh affairs and tribute of its products.'
idiomatic: entrust the park officer with marsh affairs and tribute of its products.'

literal: Let the responsible offices assess the people within the capital region, making households without cattle exchange human and bovine labor to open fields, hoe, and weed.
idiomatic: Let offices assess the capital region, having households without cattle exchange human and ox labor to open fields.

literal: Where there is a cattle household and a household without cattle, one person plants twenty-two mu and is compensated with seven mu of private hoeing labor, [7] with gradations accordingly; for small and elderly households without cattle, seven mu are planted and small and elderly repay with two mu of hoeing.
idiomatic: Where one has cattle and one does not, one person plants twenty-two mu for seven mu of hoeing, [7] by gradation; small and elderly without cattle plant seven mu and repay two mu.

literal: All take households of five mouths or fewer in poverty as the standard.
idiomatic: All take poor households of five mouths or fewer as standard.

literal: Each lists households by mouth count and urged planting in mu, clearly setting ledger accounts.
idiomatic: Each lists households, urged planting, and sets ledgers.

literal: What is planted is marked at the field head with name to distinguish sowing merit.
idiomatic: Planters mark the field head with names to distinguish merit.

literal: " He also forbade drinking, mixed games, and abandoning the root to peddle for profit.
idiomatic: He also forbade drinking, mixed games, and peddling over farming.

literal: Opened fields were greatly increased.
idiomatic: Opened fields greatly increased.

literal: Zhengping year 1, sixth month, day wuchen: he died in the Eastern Palace at age twenty-four.
idiomatic: In Zhengping year 1, on the wuchen day of the sixth month, he died in the Eastern Palace at twenty-four.

literal: Day gengwu: the patent of enfeoffment said: "Alas!
idiomatic: On the gengwu day the patent said: "Alas!

literal: You were born with bright wisdom and precocious insight from youth.
idiomatic: You were born bright and precocious from youth.

literal: You took the position of the young yang and bore the foundation.
idiomatic: You took the young yang and bore the foundation.

literal: Guest at the four gates, the hundred duties were in order;
idiomatic: Guest at the four gates, the hundred duties were ordered;

literal: you truly regulated the myriad tasks; wind and rain did not go astray.
idiomatic: you regulated the myriad tasks; wind and rain did not stray.

literal: You should have enjoyed boundless years and elevated Our royal fortune—how is it that misfortune came and you suddenly died? We are stricken with grief in Our heart!
idiomatic: You should have enjoyed boundless years—how misfortune came and you died! We are stricken in heart!

literal: Now We send the credential-bearing commissioner Concurrent Grand Commandant Zhang Li and Concurrent Chancellor of State Dou Jin with the patent to grant at the bier the posthumous title "Jingmu," to display your bright virtue.
idiomatic: We send Zhang Li, Concurrent Grand Commandant, and Dou Jin, Concurrent Chancellor of State, to grant at the bier the posthumous title Jingmu.

literal: If your soul has awareness, honor this."
idiomatic: If your soul has awareness, honor this."

literal: When Gaozong took the throne he posthumously honored him as Emperor Jingmu Gongzong; temple name Gongzong.
idiomatic: When Gaozong took the throne he honored him as Emperor Jingmu Gongzong; temple name Gongzong.

literal: The historian says: Shizu was intelligent, heroic, and resolute, majestic and outstanding; with the resources of two reigns he roused the spirit of conquest and then the war chariot went forth on four sides, turning through peril and ease.
idiomatic: The historian says: Shizu was intelligent, heroic, and resolute; with two reigns' resources he roused conquest; the war chariot went four ways through peril and ease.

literal: He swept Tongwan, pacified Qin and Long, cut Liaohai, cleared the river source; southern barbarians bore burdens, northern Rouran were cut down; the four quarters were settled and barbarian and Chinese were unified—his achievement was great.
idiomatic: He swept Tongwan, pacified Qin and Long, cut Liaohai, cleared the river source; south bore burdens, north Rouran were cut; the four quarters were settled and barbarian and Chinese unified—his achievement was great.

literal: Thus the enterprise of Wei shone beyond the hundred kings—is this not divine wisdom and planning, a mandate for the age?
idiomatic: Thus Wei's enterprise shone beyond the hundred kings—is this not divine wisdom and a mandate for the age?

literal: Yet at the start the eastern heir did not reach the end; at the last a breach arose from what was neglected.
idiomatic: Yet at the start the eastern heir did not finish; at the last breach arose from neglect.

literal: To secure the root and leave forethought—was this not unconsidered?
idiomatic: To secure the root and leave forethought—was this unconsidered?

literal: Gongzong had bright virtue and fine repute yet died young in successive ages—is this not the grief of the Park of Li?
idiomatic: Gongzong had bright virtue yet died young—is this not the grief of the Park of Li?

literal: Collation notes
idiomatic: Collation notes

literal: Fifth month: all editions read "fifth month" as "third month."
idiomatic: Fifth month: all editions read "fifth month" as "third month."

literal: Since above already records the fourth month, now according to Cefu juan 112
idiomatic: Since the fourth month is already recorded above, now according to Cefu juan 112

literal: 〈page 1339〉
changed.
idiomatic: changed.

literal: Traveled to Lu: all editions have a note "deficient" below.
idiomatic: Traveled to Lu: all editions note "deficient" below.

literal: Zizhi Tongjian juan 124
idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian juan 124

literal: 〈page 3905〉
reads "the Wei ruler came to Lu."
idiomatic: reads "the Wei ruler came to Lu."

literal: Thus Sima Guang did not regard there as being lacuna.
idiomatic: Thus Sima Guang did not regard the text as deficient.

literal: Divided troops to raid Linjin and Bayi: Zizhi Tongjian juan 124
idiomatic: Divided troops to raid Linjin and Bayi: Zizhi Tongjian juan 124

literal: 〈page 3915〉
Hu Sanxing's note:
idiomatic: Hu Sanxing's note:

literal: 〈abbreviated below as Hu note〉
idiomatic: (abbreviated below as Hu note)
